instructions:
The principal wants a yes/no answer. Using ONLY the listed fields (refer to each as
latest("<ref>")), write a decision rule as a boolean expression with explicit thresholds, the conventional or
physical reason for each threshold, and short labels for yes and no. The rationale must hold on any day: do not
mention today's values in it. If an existing service already gives a
direct verdict or index, you may use it, but prefer rules that remain correct if one source is missing (use 'or' /
'and' deliberately). A field that holds several numbers (e.g. hourly values "30 20 10 0") can be given to max(),
min() or sum(), e.g. max(latest("src:field")) >= 50. Allowed functions: latest, max, min, sum, round, coalesce,
if_else, max_over, min_over. Do not invent fields. One or two rules at most.

exclude: Overnight and evening hours outside the drying period
Forecasts for other days or other cities
questions.quantity: Verdict on whether outdoor line-drying today in Osaka is suitable, based on forecast conditions over the daytime drying period: chance/amount of precipitation, humidity, wind, temperature/sunshine. Verdict plus the key reasons.
questions.question: Is today a good day to dry laundry outside in Osaka?
questions.population: Osaka city, today's daytime hours (local time, roughly 08:00-18:00)

payload.instruction: Each rule above was rejected for the stated reason. Values are compared as numbers only when they are numbers (a unit suffix like '%' is stripped); compare text values with ==. Write a rule that evaluates now.

rules.question: Is today a good day to dry laundry outside in Osaka?
rules.yes_label: Yes: a wind forecast is issued, so no wind-based obstacle is identified
rules.no_label: No/unknown: no wind forecast available, so suitability cannot be confirmed
rules.rationale: The only available field is JMA's qualitative wind text for Osaka, which carries no rain, humidity or sunshine information. Wind is one factor in drying: light to moderate breeze speeds drying, while very strong wind can blow laundry off the line. The text has no numeric speed and cannot be substring-matched with the allowed functions, so this rule only checks that a forecast exists. It is a weak wind-only proxy, not a full verdict, and should be combined with precipitation and humidity data when available.

thresholds.why: A published wind forecast is required to make any wind-based judgment; no numeric threshold is possible because the field is qualitative text.
